stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt cap is reached, and
reaching the cap is charged the full cap. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until

---
name: continual-arc
description: Solve Continual-ARC puzzles, maintain per-task transforms, and recover after incorrect submissions.

# Continual ARC

For a Continual-ARC instance with a task id and test grid:

1. Check `programs/<task id>.py`. If present, run `transform(test_grid)` and submit its exact result before any other task action. Otherwise request demonstrations as needed, preserving plausible competing rules until examples distinguish them. After an incorrect verdict, do not infer the alternative from a failed guess alone: identify the exact submitted candidate, compare it with a fresh run, and test concrete alternatives against every complete demo. Keep the incumbent rule until an alternative reproduces all demos exactly; request another demo only when it discriminates between those alternatives. For geometric ray/line tasks, explicitly model which cells a line traverses, whether marks/objects block or are overwritten, whether source objects remain intact, and how perpendicular intersections are handled; compare candidate policies to every output before coding.
2. Infer transformations from complete input-output pairs, comparing all cells and dimensions. Track colors, objects, dividers, background, and edges. For color-only tasks, derive an explicit input-color→output-color table from each full pair and compare the tables across demos; do not assume a role-based recoloring such as “background stays” or “marker becomes zero.” If demos show the same palette mapped consistently, apply that exact table to the test. Otherwise request a pair that distinguishes candidate mappings before extrapolating. For patterns, test orientation, period, phase, and palette independently; do not extrapolate a visually plausible motif. For repeated grids, determine periods and whether output samples cells, intersections, regions, or boundaries. For reflections/tilings, verify placements and orientations on full examples. When outputs appear to color a figure as a set of repeated pieces, enumerate candidate piece placements and color/orientation signatures, then exact-cover the foreground cells; run the solver against every demo before using its test output. Do not rely on a plausible greedy tiling when pieces overlap or multiple coverings exist. For fills, compare 4/8-neighbor connectivity, seeds, boundaries, stopping conditions, and the exact recoloring mask; do not assume every reachable cell changes. For line gap-fills, separately verify single-mark behavior, between-mark intervals, and whether rows, columns, or both are affected.
3. Implement `transform(grid)` only when one coherent rule reproduces every available pair exactly. After each change, run it against complete demonstrations and test input; compare all cells and dimensions, including every row length, and validate value range. Do not submit an unverified candidate unless demos are exhausted. Derive the action grid directly from the current program run, emit/parse compact JSON, and submit that exact output—never manually reconstruct or adjust it. Keep runner data in the workspace, not `/tmp`.
4. Take exactly one task action per turn (`submit`, `request_demos`, or, after completion, `finish`) with its JSON object on the final line. After a correct verdict, save the verified transform to `programs/<task id>.py` and finish. If demos run out without verification, submit the strongest supported candidate without calling it verified.
